library.name: Vanilla Sponge (adapted)
library.label: Adapted version
library.scaledHow: Source batch ~1,068 g raw batter, scaled to 1 kg baked cake (92% yield).
method: Heat the oven to 175°C. Grease and line two 8-inch tins.
Stir milk with vinegar and rest a few minutes so it thickens slightly.
Whisk in sugar, oil and vanilla until the sugar mostly dissolves.
Sift flour, cornstarch, baking powder, baking soda and salt into the bowl and mix just until smooth.
Divide between the tins and bake 20–22 minutes, until the tops spring back. Cool fully before filling or frosting.

library.name: Chocolate Sponge (adapted)
library.label: Adapted version
library.scaledHow: Source batch ~1,165 g raw batter. Hot coffee/water is counted in the batter but not costed in her original sheet; this adapted version costs a small amount of brewed coffee / hot water at an estimated price. Light + cane sugar are entered as granulated sugar, matching her sheet.
method: Heat the oven to 175°C. Grease and line two 8-inch tins.
Mix milk and vinegar; rest 5 minutes.
Whisk in both sugars (here, all granulated), oil and vanilla.
Sift flour, cocoa, baking soda, baking powder and salt; fold into the wet mix until smooth.
Stir in hot coffee or boiling water to bloom the cocoa, split between tins, and bake 25–30 minutes. Cool completely.
library.notes: Coffee is optional for flavour; boiling water works. Confirm the estimated coffee price before using this cost.

library.name: Red Velvet Sponge (adapted)
library.label: Adapted version
library.scaledHow: Source batch ~1,198 g raw batter, scaled to 1 kg. Her cream cheese frosting is a separate recipe.
method: Heat the oven to 175°C. Grease and line two 8-inch tins.
Combine milk, yogurt and vinegar; rest until slightly curdled.
Whisk in oil, sugar, vanilla and red gel colour.
Sift flour, cocoa, cornstarch, baking soda and salt; mix in just until smooth.
Bake 30–40 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool fully, then level the tops before frosting.

library.name: Coconut Sponge (adapted)
library.label: Adapted version
library.sourceName: PastrybySaloni — Mango Coconut Cake (coconut sponge only)
library.scaledHow: Taken from the coconut sponge in her Mango Coconut Cake. Batch ~1,012 g, scaled to 1 kg. Lemon juice in the source is swapped for white vinegar, matching her existing recipe.
method: Heat the oven to 175°C. Grease and line two 8-inch tins.
Stir milk, vinegar (or lemon juice) and yogurt; rest briefly.
Whisk in oil, sugar and vanilla, then stir through desiccated coconut.
Sift flour, cornstarch, baking powder, baking soda and salt; mix until just smooth.
Bake 25–30 minutes until springy. Cool, then level before filling.

library.name: Swiss Meringue Buttercream (adapted)
library.label: Adapted version — standard ratio, not from PastrybySaloni
library.scaledHow: Egg whites are about 5 per kg; costed at the whole-egg price (slightly high).
method: Warm egg whites with the sugar over a gentle water bath, stirring until the sugar dissolves and the mix is hot to the touch.
Whip to a glossy, cool meringue.
Beat in soft butter a little at a time, then vanilla and salt, until smooth and silky.
If it looks curdled, keep beating; if too soft, chill briefly and beat again.

library.name: Mascarpone Cream (adapted)
library.label: Adapted version — standard whipped mascarpone cream, not from PastrybySaloni
library.scaledHow: Mascarpone + whipping cream + icing sugar, per 1 kg.
method: Chill the bowl. Soften the mascarpone briefly so it is smooth but still cool.
Whip the cream with icing sugar and vanilla to soft peaks.
Fold the mascarpone through the cream until thick and spreadable. Do not over-whip.
Use the same day, or keep chilled and re-stir gently before spreading.
